assumptions: Capture reagents and particle-count instruments have sufficient sensitivity and compatibility for fraction-level measurements and low-biomass in vivo samples (lavage/CSF).
Exogenous spike-in controls will be used to separate assay recovery failures from true absence of endogenous intact-EV signal.
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 and rodent intranasal efficacy reports identify source-cell-dependent variability in EV-associated signals and emphasize orthogonal intact-EV analytics. Large-animal intranasal biodistribution suggests delivery and/or particle integrity barriers that could be influenced by source-cell state. Distinguishing senescence mechanisms may reveal a reproducible link between source-cell biology and membrane-protected EV signatures relevant to intranasal exposure.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative pass/fail for preserved orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive signal) plus detectable in vivo recoverable capture signal in nasal lavage/CSF/tissue after intranasal dosing.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Source-cell senescence mechanism (replicative vs SASP-induced)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Operationalizing senescence mechanism (p16/p21 expression and SASP profile) may stratify lots by intact-EV analytical signature and short-interval in vivo recoverability, enabling an MCB/WCB gating attribute.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: High: plausible but unproven causal link; requires spike-in controlled orthogonal experiments and in vivo bridging.

edges.competing_explanation: Culture conditions, donor genetics, or purification artifacts (not senescence) could explain observed differences.
edges.missing_experiment: Program-specific orthogonal intact-EV comparison across senescence mechanisms with spike-in recovery controls.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: guidance and preclinical reports support source-dependent composition effects but do not define senescence mechanism as causal.

edges.competing_explanation: Lack of in vivo detection may result from administration route, formulation, labeling, or species clearance rather than source-cell-dependent particle integrity.
edges.missing_experiment: Matched short-interval in vivo dosing and orthogonal intact-EV verification comparing materials from early- versus late-passage MSCs.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: limited large-animal biodistribution data suggest delivery barriers that could confound intact-EV recoverability, but do not prove senescence as the causal factor.

nodes.statement: Donor-MSC senescence mechanism (replicative-passage high p16/p21 versus induced SASP-rich senescence) alters features of released particle populations (membrane integrity, surface-marker accessibility, particle:protein ratio).

These senescence-linked particle features produce distinct orthogonal intact-EV analytical signatures (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) that can be measured in source material.

Materials from source cells with a favorable intact-EV signature are more likely to produce short-interval in vivo evidence of intact-EV presence in nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa after intranasal dosing than materials from senescent or SASP-rich sources.

competing_explanations: Differences in intact-EV recovery reflect downstream processing (TFF, formulation, device) rather than intrinsic source-cell senescence.
Apparent conserved markers reflect co-isolation of non-vesicular complexes and not membrane-protected EV cargo.
dependencies: Analytical validation of capture reagent compatibility and spike-in tracer performance
Sufficient material yield from characterized source-cell lots
Approval for short-interval animal sampling protocols
design_question: Does donor-MSC senescence mechanism (replicative vs SASP-rich induced) causally alter orthogonal intact-EV identity signatures and short-interval nasal→CSF/olfactory-mucosa recoverability after matched intranasal dosing?
expected_measurable_effect: Early-passage/replicative-stable MSC lots will show orthogonal intact-EV signatures (capture-positive particle-peak co-localization, detergent/protease sensitivity, protected-cargo signals) and yield reproducible short-interval recoverable intact-EV signal in lavage/CSF/tissue after intranasal dosing, whereas SASP-rich or late-passage senescent lots will not.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow combined with short-interval in vivo sampling: (1) add spike-in prior to fractionation; (2) density-fractionation or SEC with particle counting per fraction; (3) immuno-capture on intact fractions with separate readouts for spike-in and endogenous markers; (4) protease/RNase protection ± detergent on captured material; (5) quantify protected-cargo panels optionally; (6) intranasal dosing and short-interval lavage/CSF/tissue collection for orthogonal verification of exposure.
experiment.comparator: Within-donor matched comparisons across senescence states (early-passage baseline vs replicative-passage senescent vs induced SASP-rich senescent) with matched processing; include detergent+protease-disrupted aliquots and secretome-retaining controls.
experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EV preparation spiked and processed in parallel (validates capture/protection assays). Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples. Spike-in tracer used as per-sample recovery control.
dependencies: Validated capture reagents and spike-in tracer
Sufficient conditioned-medium yield for matrixed processing and in vivo arms
Animal protocol approvals and analytical capacity for low-biomass capture from lavage/CSF samples
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible qualitative difference between senescence mechanisms across replicates in orthogonal intact-EV signatures or short-interval in vivo recoverability, despite validated spike-in recovery.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If falsified, do not use senescence mechanism as a deterministic source-cell gate; prioritize alternative source/process variables or secretome-centric product definitions.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: Conditioned medium from early-passage, low p16/p21 MSCs will yield an orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive signal) and greater short-interval in vivo recoverable intact-EV evidence after matched intranasal dosing compared with conditioned medium from late-passage, high p16/p21 MSCs or SASP-induced senescent MSCs.
experiment.primary_readout: Co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and loss of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase in conditioned-medium-derived preparations; presence and relative magnitude of capture-positive signal and particle counts in short-interval lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa samples after intranasal dosing comparing senescence states.
experiment.question: Does senescence mechanism (replicative-passage high p16/p21 vs induced SASP-rich senescence) causally affect orthogonal intact-EV analytical signatures in conditioned-medium-derived preparations and short-interval in vivo recoverable intact-EV signal after intranasal dosing when assay recovery is controlled by spike-in?
required_material: Donor-matched MSC cultures expanded to produce: early-passage (low p16/p21), replicative-passage high p16/p21, and induced SASP-rich senescent lots (oxidative stress/irradiation) where feasible
Conditioned medium from each source lot processed identically into: (A) enriched small-EV fraction and (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining)
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) for within-sample recovery control
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5) and capture-compatibility buffer panels
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Protease (proteinase K), RNase reagents and detergent (Triton X-100) for membrane-disruption controls
Short-interval in vivo rodent dosing capability with collection of nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-mucosa/olfactory-bulb-adjacent tissue at predefined short post-dose intervals
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
secondary_readouts: Spike-in recovery percentage per fraction (qualitative recovered & membrane-protected vs not recovered)
Protein:particle ratio differences between senescence conditions
Protected-cargo panel (optional) presence/absence in capture-positive fractions
Reproducibility across biological replicates (>=3 conditioned-medium lots per senescence condition)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across >=3 independent donor-matched preparations, materials from one senescence mechanism (e.g., early-passage replicative-stable) reproducibly show (A) capture-positive particle-peak co-localization and detergent/protease-sensitive captured signal in source material and (B) detectable capture-positive signal and particle co-localization in short-interval lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa samples after intranasal dosing; materials from the contrasting senescence mechanism (e.g., SASP-induced) reproducibly fail these criteria.

explicit_inferences: Orthogonal intact-EV analytics (capture, particle co-localization, detergent/protease protection) are necessary to classify a preparation as EV-enriched and to gate downstream CMC actions.
Source-cell senescence mechanism is a falsifiable candidate driver of measurable intact-EV attributes relevant for intranasal delivery.
falsification_criteria: No reproducible difference between early- and late-passage or SASP-induced senescence source materials in orthogonal intact-EV signatures or in short-interval in vivo recoverability across >=3 independent replicates, when spike-in controls validate assay recovery.
Spike-in controls fail to validate assay recovery across replicates (methodological failure) that prevents discrimination.
human_decisions_required: Select senescence operational definitions and thresholds (p16/p21 cutoffs; SASP panel components) for MCB/WCB qualification if hypothesis supported
Approve spike-in tracer choice and assays for orthogonal workflow
Authorize resource allocation for ≥3 pilot lots and in vivo bridging experiments
manufacturability_assessment: If supported, specifying senescence-mechanism criteria for MCB/WCB selection is manufacturable (defines cell-bank acceptance and upstream controls) but requires investment in orthogonal assay validation and pilot GMP-like lots to demonstrate reproducibility and yield.
manufacturing_rationale: If senescence mechanism deterministically affects membrane integrity or surface-phenotype of released particles, then specifying source-cell senescence as an MCB/WCB attribute enables targeted CMC controls (bank selection, batch acceptance, and downstream process envelopes) and reduces wasted scale-up effort on non-viable lots.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow with exogenous spike-in controls applied across matched lots and senescence conditions, plus short-interval intranasal dosing in rodents for in vivo→ex vivo bridging. Key readouts: capture-positive particle-peak co-localization, detergent/protease sensitivity, protected-cargo panel, spike-in recovery, and recoverable signal in lavage/CSF/tissue.
novelty_statement: This proposal distinguishes senescence mechanism (replicative versus SASP-induced) as the substantive source-cell attribute to test for causal effects on intact-EV identity and short-interval intranasal recoverability. This is a substantive change from merely labeling 'senescence state' by passage number: it requires experimentally induced SASP-type senescence and within-donor matched comparisons to separate mechanistic drivers (SASP biology) from chronological passage effects, and mandates spike-in-controlled orthogonal in vivo bridging experiments to discriminate assay failures from true biological absence of intact EVs.
principal_risks: Assay sensitivity and capture-compatibility limitations could produce false negatives in orthogonal workflows.
Large-animal intranasal biodistribution limitations may persist even if source-cell gating is optimized.
Resource/time cost for generating pilot GMP-like lots and validating orthogonal assays before regulatory engagement.
proposed_potency_relationship: If a membrane-protected particle-associated signature is reproducibly linked to a protected in vitro neuroinflammation-modulating activity and to short-interval in vivo recoverability, that signature may be used as a mechanism-linked potency gate. At present this is unproven and requires the proposed experiments.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a source-cell qualification attribute that distinguishes donor-MSCs by senescence mechanism (replicative-passage high p16/p21 versus induced SASP-rich senescence) and require orthogonal intact-EV identity verification plus short-interval in vivo recoverability as go/no-go gates for lot advancement.
title: Source-cell senescence mechanism as a gate for intact-EV identity and short-interval intranasal recoverability
